title.en: Sound waves, frequency, speed and echo

text.en: A temple bell rings and the sound travels outwards in all directions. Sound needs a medium and travels as waves of compressions and rarefactions.

Sound is produced by vibrating bodies and needs a material medium - it cannot travel in a vacuum.
Sound waves in air are longitudinal: particles vibrate along the direction of travel, forming compressions and rarefactions.
Frequency is the number of vibrations per second (hertz); the time period T = 1/f.
Speed of sound = frequency x wavelength (v = f x lambda).
Sound travels fastest in solids, slower in liquids and slowest in gases; in air at room temperature it is about 343 m/s.
Loudness depends on amplitude; pitch depends on frequency; humans hear 20 Hz to 20 000 Hz.
An echo is the reflection of sound heard after at least 0.1 s, so the obstacle must be at least about 17 m away.

problem.en: A sound has a frequency of 500 Hz and a wavelength of 0.68 m. Find its speed.

why.en: Matches the speed of sound in air.

prompt.en: Explain how sound travels and what an echo is.

points.en: Sound needs a medium and is longitudinal.
